scope: All 12 original title/abstract records; all five facets per paper; unchanged policy v2.2 and clarifications.
independence_limit: Author B's source-only draft was sealed before author A files were opened. This is an AI procedural cross-review, not two independent humans or human-gold certification.

policy_assessment.reason: The identified issues are ordinary annotation corrections under existing scope/coreference, actual-method versus validation-baseline, and artifact/finding coverage rules. Split/merge choices retaining the same meaning are advisory. Resolve the material corrections through source adjudication before accepting references or starting full annotation rollout.

problem.rationale: A1 explicitly motivates negation handling through polarity effects in sentiment analysis.

task.rationale: A0 states the survey objective; the surveyed scope is not mistaken for implemented prediction tasks.

method.rationale: The actual survey operation is retained without listing every reviewed approach as used.

dataset.rationale: No named used or introduced resource is supplied.

contribution.rationale: The presented survey is an artifact; no background claim is promoted to a new empirical result.

problem.rationale: A0 supplies the NLI antecedent for A2's explicit systematic-comparison gap.

task.rationale: A3-A4 preserve the 24 interfaces, ten sample questions, and strengths/weaknesses goal.

method.rationale: Overview, question evaluation, and categorization are actual survey procedures. Category types remain reviewed objects.

dataset.rationale: The curated question list is unnamed.

contribution.rationale: All three conclusions are supported, but their concepts should retain the database-NLI scope rather than reading as unrestricted claims about all keyword/grammar systems.

material_issues.rationale: Policy section 4 requires the scope needed to avoid a broader claim. A3 explicitly supplies NLIs for databases; adding only evidence without this scope in the concept would leave the generalization.

suggested_corrections.concept: NLIs for databases: keyword-based systems are enough to answer simple questions.
NLIs for databases: To solve more complex questions involving subqueries, the system needs to apply some sort of parsing to identify structural dependencies.
NLIs for databases: Grammar-based systems are overall the most powerful ones, but are highly dependent on their manually designed rules.

problem.rationale: The spam-volume need and weak manual keyword filters are explicit, with the filter antecedent resolved.

task.rationale: The source explicitly investigates two learning algorithms for spam filtering.

method.rationale: Naive Bayesian and memory-based methods are the primary empirical-comparison subjects. The e-mail reader's keyword filter remains only a comparator.

dataset.rationale: The public corpus is unnamed and standard benchmarks are an aspiration.

contribution.rationale: Introduced cost-sensitive measures are artifacts rather than model methods. The final finding names both algorithms and preserves spam filtering and its keyword-filter comparator.

problem.rationale: A3 supplies the Settlers of Catan expert-challenge implementation gap.

task.rationale: A0+A3 ground the policy-acquisition target in the actual game.

method.rationale: Both independent components and A2's retrieval/simulation decision procedure are present. This covers the actual integration content.
advisory_refinements: Do not add a generic 'hybrid model' method merely to mirror contribution. A2 already supplies the operational workflow, and an additional parent with only 'combines' would duplicate covered content. A richer combined workflow could replace A2, but is not necessary.

dataset.rationale: The human-play corpus is unnamed; the game is not a named dataset.

contribution.rationale: The model artifact is supported, but the short preliminary finding leaves the model unspecified and omits the implemented Settlers of Catan setting.

material_issues.rationale: The finding must identify what is hybrid and retain the preliminary experiment's application setting. A1 remains only a superiority hypothesis.

suggested_corrections.concept: We propose a hybrid model for automatically acquiring a policy for a complex game, which combines online learning with mining knowledge from a corpus of human game play. We implement and assess our model in an agent playing the complex win-lose board game Settlers of Catan, which lacks an implementation that would challenge a human expert. The results from the preliminary set of experiments illustrate the potential of such a joint model.

problem.rationale: The practice antecedent and complex-domain boundary limitation are complete.

task.rationale: A3-A5 explicitly establish formal properties and A6 shows practical axiomatization. These theory/demonstration objectives are supported; A has better primary-objective coverage than B's A6-only draft.
advisory_refinements: For clearer task/contribution separation, the third task can be shortened to 'axiomatize the logical interaction between concepts and metaconcepts' [A6]. The current HiLog capability wording is source-supported, so this is a role-expression refinement rather than missing coverage.
Do not remove the formal-properties objectives merely because their proofs also produce contribution findings. They are the explicit main research activity in this theoretical paper.

method.rationale: Contextual and HiLog semantics are separately proposed. A6 also establishes HiLog's demonstration role; SHOIQ/OWL languages are analyzed objects.

dataset.rationale: Ontology languages and description logic do not establish a named used ontology dataset.

contribution.rationale: Both semantics and all three findings retain their subjects, undecidability cause, either-semantics condition, and HiLog antecedent.

problem.rationale: The shared-gene limitation retains can/may and the complex-disease condition.

task.rationale: Disease similarity and term/entity similarity targets are explicit operation-and-object phrases. A's labels say measure similarity, rather than merely present a model.
advisory_refinements: The ontology-term and annotated-entity goals can remain as distinct computational targets, or be treated as mechanism scope under the overall disease task. This granularity choice alone is not a material role error; do not add duplicate generic tasks.

method.rationale: A4-A5 introduce the similarity functions for the disease-similarity objective. A7-A8 validate that proposed method with a benchmark, rather than establish a standalone research objective comparing baseline techniques.

material_issues.rationale: The policy permits comparison subjects as methods when comparative assessment is itself the research objective. Here the paper presents a new similarity method and uses exact matches/gene overlap to validate it. Being executed as a comparator is insufficient by itself; keep both comparators in the A8 contribution finding.

dataset.rationale: GO is explicitly defined and actually used as the Gene Ontology structured resource.
advisory_refinements: Prefer the source full name 'Gene Ontology' [A7] for a less ambiguous standalone resource label. This is a source-defined alias refinement, not an invented resource.

contribution.rationale: Both target levels are present in the introduced function family; A6's generic comparison preserves its unknown comparator rather than guessing it. A8-A10 retain all conditions and numbers.
advisory_refinements: Splitting the functions artifact into term-level and annotated-entity-level items is permissible but not a material correction: the combined item already retains both targets and the shared co-occurrence/information-content basis.
Retain A8 exactly, including gene overlap's higher recall. Do not reinterpret the source's broad 'performed better' claim as superiority on every metric.

problem.rationale: The lack of human-labeled resources is an explicit motivation.

task.rationale: The source states a survey of typological information in NLP development.

method.rationale: Only the literature survey is treated as performed; advocacy and possible induction developments remain future direction.

dataset.rationale: No typological database name is supplied.

contribution.rationale: The combined performance/explanation finding preserves to-date scope, modest gains, both database limits, and under-utilization. The causal link makes this grouping acceptable; B's split form is not inherently superior.

problem.rationale: No explicit prior limitation is stated; later training-time cost is not retrofitted as motivation.

task.rationale: A1 directly states empirical comparison on the word-order task.

method.rationale: Both actual comparison subjects and their evaluated combination are covered; names and anaphoric links are grounded.

dataset.rationale: Raw text and the standard benchmark are unnamed.

contribution.rationale: The first three findings and the final combination result lose the word-order setting, making the language-model claims broader than the experiment.

material_issues.rationale: The quality impact, raw-text benefit, performance/time tradeoff, and best-result claims are results of the A1 word-order comparison. The error-distribution finding already says in word ordering.

suggested_corrections.concept: word order task: the quality of automatically-parsed training data has a relatively small impact on syntactic models.
word order task: Both of syntactic and N-gram models can benefit from large-scale raw text.
word order task: Compared with N-gram models, syntactic models give overall better performance, but they require much more training time.
N-gram and syntactic language models on word order task: A combination of the two models integrates the advantages of each model, achieving the best result in a standard benchmark.

problem.rationale: The source presents an investigation, while observed bias is a result rather than a prior asserted limitation.

task.rationale: Quality, time, automatic pre-annotation, manual POS annotation, and bias are retained.

method.rationale: The comparative annotation protocol contains both from-scratch and pre-annotation conditions without labeling humans as techniques.

dataset.rationale: Penn Treebank corpus is explicitly named and annotated; the citation year is not a version.

contribution.rationale: The actual corpus context is present, but POS annotation should be explicit so quality and speed results do not read as claims about arbitrary annotation.

material_issues.rationale: A0 supplies the manual part-of-speech annotation scope. The quality-gain/bias grouping can remain: its while-clause preserves the source's linked caveat.

suggested_corrections.concept: manual part-of-speech annotation of the Penn Treebank corpus under various experimental setups, either from scratch or using various pre-annotations: These experiments confirm and detail the gain in quality observed before, while showing that biases do appear and should be taken into account.

manual part-of-speech annotation of the Penn Treebank corpus under various experimental setups, either from scratch or using various pre-annotations: even a not so accurate tagger can help improving annotation speed.
